Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola sketched below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224890/assets/e5393f15ff154f1f4cc310791790db0fe0ad0d9faa076d10f3f6ec7b481de086.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
From the graph, we deduce that the roots are $x_1=-3$ and $x_2=2.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2}=\frac{-3+2}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}.$
